title: Landing y catálogo
brief: Landing page for an Apple products store in Argentina (es-AR), with a family entry point, a product grid and — in two of the three directions — the product-detail treatment with a capacity selector. All prices are sample data rendered in ARS.

artboards.title: Galería
artboards.tradeoff: White gallery wall with no tiles under the photos: works hang at different heights, each with a hairline wall label whose tick extends on hover, and the monumental iMac is captioned at numeral scale. Faithful to Apple and the quietest of the three; six works still hide the other 58 and it carries the least information per screen.
artboards.signature: The wall label: a 1px tick that is short until you hover the work, then draws to the full caption width.

artboards.title: Índice
artboards.tradeoff: A printed index: the family list is a ruled numeral spine (01–06) and the catalogue heading carries the real count of products as a figure that counts up as it enters. The hero photograph crosses the full-bleed rule instead of sitting in its own panel. Dense and readable; reads closer to an editorial catalogue than to Apple, and the capacity ladder lives outside the product page.
artboards.signature: The counted figure: 64 set inside the sentence, counting from 0 as it scrolls into view, above a numeral spine that draws itself.

artboards.title: Vitrina
artboards.tradeoff: A black floor with lit cases: the hero case leaves the content column and is cropped by the viewport, the price is the second display line of the title, and the catalogue puts one case at 2x2 against five at 1x1. The strongest premium pull; the darkest and the furthest from a familiar Argentine store.
artboards.signature: The case that leaves the page: the lit case runs off the right edge of the window, so the product sits in light that keeps going.

artboards.title: Detalle · Galería
artboards.tradeoff: The product page as the same white wall: the work hangs with no tile, its wall label (name, then one caption line) is the page's h1, and the four real photos sit under it as a numbered strip of small labels. The capacity selector and the one variant price live in the margin column. Quietest and most legible; the label copy carries a lot and the page gives the configurator little drama.
artboards.signature: The wall label: the short 1px tick draws to the full caption width on hover or keyboard focus, and every photo keeps its own small label.

artboards.title: Detalle · Índice
artboards.tradeoff: The product page as one entry of the printed index: photos are numbered plates 01-04 down a ruled spine, capacities are a ruled ladder 01-03 that marks the chosen one with the word 'Elegida' and not only with colour, and the headline carries 3 counted from 0 as it enters. Dense and comparable at a glance; the most textual of the three and the last to feel like a store.
artboards.signature: The counted figure: three capacities set inside the headline, counting up as it scrolls into view, above a numeral spine that draws itself.

artboards.title: Detalle · Vitrina
artboards.tradeoff: The product page on the black floor: the product sits in a lit case that leaves the content column and is cropped by the viewport, the variant price is the second display line of the block, and the four photos are small lit cases under a dark segmented capacity control. The strongest premium pull; the darkest, and a dark segmented pill is the least familiar control for an Argentine buyer.
artboards.signature: The case that leaves the page: the lit case runs off the right edge of the window, so the product sits in light that keeps going.

note: Revision 2 (bolder pass): same palette, same three bets, larger display scale, one monument and one signature detail per direction. The standalone product page now exists in all three directions (04-06): same page, same real product, same three capacities and the same disabled cart, so the detail treatment can be compared across bets.
